quests.instruction: Leave an ice pop in the sun and it melts into a puddle. Put orange juice in the freezer overnight and it will…
quests.hint: Think about how ice pops are made at home.
quests.explanation: Melting turns a solid into a liquid when it warms up. Freezing does the reverse: a liquid turns solid when it gets very cold.
quests.funFact: Water is unusual because it expands when it freezes, which is why ice floats.

quests.instruction: To charge a tablet, you plug it in. When the battery is full, you ___ it.
quests.hint: Think of what you do with the cable once charging is done.
quests.explanation: Plugging in connects a device to the power. Unplugging disconnects it.
quests.funFact: Wall sockets with different shapes are used in different countries, so travelers often carry adapters.

quests.instruction: At night, Nani locks the front door. In the morning, she uses the same key to ___ it.
quests.hint: Besides keeping a door shut, what else can a key do?
quests.explanation: Locking secures something so it can’t be opened. Unlocking releases it again.
quests.funFact: Some of the oldest known locks were wooden ones used in ancient Egypt.

quests.instruction: Kofi forgot his eraser, so he asked Ana if he could borrow hers. Ana agreed to ___ it to him.
quests.hint: Who gives the eraser and who takes it for a while?
quests.explanation: Borrowing and lending are two sides of the same trade: one person takes something for a while, the other lets them have it.
quests.funFact: Libraries let you borrow books for free for a set number of weeks.

quests.instruction: Monday to Friday are weekdays. Saturday and Sunday make up the…
quests.hint: Which two days do many children spend at home instead of school?
quests.explanation: Weekdays are the working or school days of the week. The weekend is the pair of days off at the end.
quests.funFact: In some countries, the weekend falls on Friday and Saturday instead.

quests.instruction: On the nature trail, the guide walks in front to lead the way. The children walk behind and ___ her.
quests.hint: Where do you walk if you’re not the one in front?
quests.explanation: To lead is to go first and show the way. To follow is to come behind and go where the leader goes.
quests.funFact: Geese flying in a V take turns being the leader at the front.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “ripe”? (a golden mango that smells sweet vs. a hard green one still on the branch)
quests.hint: Which mango would you wait a few more days to eat?
quests.explanation: Ripe fruit is ready to eat: soft, sweet and fully colored. Unripe fruit still needs more time to grow.
quests.funFact: Bananas and mangoes keep ripening after they’re picked.

quests.instruction: A lion in the jungle is wild. A cat curled up on your sofa is…
quests.hint: One animal curls up beside you; the other would run if you reached out.
quests.explanation: Wild animals live free and avoid people. Tame ones are used to humans and live safely with them.
quests.funFact: Dogs were probably the first animals that people tamed, many thousands of years ago.

quests.instruction: In class, you walk across the floor. The fan that spins above your head is fixed to the…
quests.hint: Which part of the room is directly above you?
quests.explanation: The floor is the surface under your feet. The ceiling is the surface overhead.
quests.funFact: Michelangelo painted the ceiling of the Sistine Chapel, lying on scaffolding for years.

quests.instruction: At the zoo, a green sign says “Entrance” over the way in. Over the way out, the sign says…
quests.hint: Which sign tells you how to leave?
quests.explanation: An entrance is the way into a place. An exit is the way out.
quests.funFact: Many buildings keep exit signs lit so people can always find the way out.

quests.instruction: Mum poured the sand and the pebbles into one bucket. Now Dev uses a sieve to pull the pebbles out so they’re…
quests.hint: A sieve lets small bits fall through and holds the big ones back.
quests.explanation: To mix is to put different things together. To separate is to pull them apart again.
quests.funFact: A sieve sorts by size: small bits fall through and bigger bits stay behind.

quests.instruction: It’s snowing, so we put on our gloves. When we step into the warm classroom, we…
quests.hint: What do you do with a coat when you’re too warm?
quests.explanation: Putting on means wearing something. Taking it off means removing it.
quests.funFact: Mittens often keep fingers warmer than gloves because the fingers share heat.

quests.instruction: Sasha stuck a shiny sticker on her notebook. When she wanted it gone, she carefully…
quests.hint: How do you remove a sticker without tearing it?
quests.explanation: Sticking attaches something with glue. Peeling pulls it away from the surface.
quests.funFact: Sticky notes were invented by accident, when scientists made a glue that was too weak to hold things for good.

quests.instruction: Plants grow taller every week. A woolly jumper washed in very hot water may…
quests.hint: Grandma says wool and hot dryers don’t mix.
quests.explanation: Growing means getting bigger. Shrinking means getting smaller.
quests.funFact: Wool shrinks in hot water because its fibers have tiny scales that lock together.

quests.instruction: Aunt Rina heats the milk for her chai. A cake straight from the oven is too hot to ice, so she lets it…
quests.hint: What do you do with a tray that’s too hot to touch?
quests.explanation: To heat is to make something warmer. To cool is to let it lose that warmth.
quests.funFact: Metal pans warm up and cool down faster than glass or ceramic ones.

quests.instruction: The music was too loud for the baby, so Dad turned the volume down. Later, the baby woke and the song was too quiet, so he…
quests.hint: Which way do you twist a knob when you can’t hear properly?
quests.explanation: Turning something up makes it stronger or louder. Turning it down makes it weaker or softer.
quests.funFact: Loudness is measured in decibels.

quests.instruction: Hana sends a postcard to her cousin in Delhi. A few days later, her cousin will…
quests.hint: Picture the mailbox at the other end of the journey.
quests.explanation: Sending is passing something on to another person. Receiving is getting what they sent.
quests.funFact: The Penny Black, the world’s first postage stamp, appeared in Britain in 1840.

quests.instruction: Mr. Khan wrote the date on the whiteboard. At the end of the day, the cleaner will ___ it.
quests.hint: What gets rid of marker ink with a few wipes?
quests.explanation: Writing leaves marks behind. Erasing removes them.
quests.funFact: Before rubber erasers, people sometimes rubbed out pencil marks with bread.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “add”? (5 + 3 = 8 vs. 8 − 3 = 5)
quests.hint: What do you do to the number of stickers when you give some away?
quests.explanation: To add is to put quantities together. To subtract is to take some away.
quests.funFact: The plus and minus signs were already printed in math books more than five hundred years ago.

quests.instruction: 2, 4, 6 and 8 are even numbers. 1, 3, 5 and 7 are…
quests.hint: Split each number into two equal groups and see which ones leave a spare.
quests.explanation: Even numbers split evenly into twos. Odd numbers always leave one left over.
quests.funFact: Zero counts as an even number.

quests.instruction: Tia’s glass holds more juice than Leo’s. That means Leo’s glass holds ___ juice than Tia’s.
quests.hint: Compare the two glasses side by side. Whose is lower?
quests.explanation: More means a bigger amount. Less means a smaller amount.
quests.funFact: The symbols > and < look like a mouth opening toward the bigger number.

quests.instruction: On the playground, Kabir throws the ball high. His partner’s job is to…
quests.hint: What do you do with your hands when a ball comes flying toward you?
quests.explanation: Throwing sends something through the air. Catching grabs it when it arrives.
quests.funFact: A boomerang comes back to the thrower because of its shape and spin.

quests.instruction: Every morning at school, the caretaker raises the flag. In the evening, he ___ it.
quests.hint: Watch the rope: at sunset it moves the opposite way from sunrise.
quests.explanation: To raise is to lift something up higher. To lower is to bring it back down.
quests.funFact: A pulley lets you lift a heavy object by pulling a rope downward.

quests.instruction: Ria picked up her backpack to leave. At home, she was tired, so she…
quests.hint: What do you do with something heavy when you reach home?
quests.explanation: Picking up means lifting something into your hands. Putting down means placing it back.
quests.funFact: Backpacks are best worn over both shoulders so the weight is spread evenly.

quests.instruction: At the bus stop, the children get on in a line. When the bus reaches school, they all…
quests.hint: What happens at the school gate?
quests.explanation: Getting on means stepping up into a vehicle. Getting off means stepping out of it.
quests.funFact: The first school buses in the United States were horse-drawn wagons.

quests.instruction: In autumn, we gather the fallen leaves into a pile. One strong gust of wind will ___ them.
quests.hint: Wind loves light things. Imagine a heap of dry leaves in a strong gust.
quests.explanation: Gathering brings things together in one place. Scattering sends them flying apart in all directions.
quests.funFact: Maple seeds have little wings so the wind can scatter them far from the tree.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “raw”? (a crunchy carrot stick vs. a carrot boiled soft in the stew)
quests.hint: What has been heated on a stove or in an oven?
quests.explanation: Raw food hasn’t been cooked. Cooked food has been heated until it’s changed.
quests.funFact: Cooking carrots makes some of their nutrients easier for your body to absorb.

quests.instruction: In spring, Grandpa plants tomato seedlings. When the tomatoes turn red in summer, he…
quests.hint: What do you do to a tomato that’s ready to eat?
quests.explanation: Planting puts something into the ground to grow. Picking takes it off the plant once it’s ready.
quests.funFact: A tomato is botanically a fruit, even though we usually treat it like a vegetable.

quests.instruction: Zoe hung up her paintings for Parents’ Day. When the day was over, her teacher asked her to…
quests.hint: When the event ends, the paintings don’t stay on the wall forever.
quests.explanation: Hanging up puts something on a wall to show. Taking it down removes it again.
quests.funFact: The Mona Lisa hangs in the Louvre museum in Paris.

quests.instruction: Which word is the opposite of “whole”? (an orange with its skin on vs. an orange cut cleanly in two)
quests.hint: What are you left with after you slice a pie evenly into two?
quests.explanation: Whole means all of something in one piece. Half means just one of two equal parts.
quests.funFact: A fraction like ½ means one of two equal parts.
